state.evidence: An expired certificate was observed on the mail relay host.
state.claim: The expired certificate on the TLS endpoint enables command execution.

state.evidence: The TLS scan found an expired certificate with strong ciphers otherwise negotiated.
state.claim: Remote command execution is possible through the expired TLS certificate.

state.evidence: Session cookies lack the HttpOnly flag.
state.claim: Session tokens can be stolen remotely by any attacker without user interaction.

state.evidence: The search parameter reflects input in the same response only; nothing is stored or shown to other users.
state.claim: A stored cross-site scripting vulnerability lets the attacker hijack any user session application-wide.

state.evidence: The login form lacks rate limiting; 500 attempts were accepted without lockout.
state.claim: The authentication mechanism can be bypassed entirely by brute force.

state.evidence: A directory listing exposed one backup archive that requires authentication to download.
state.claim: All server backups are publicly downloadable without authentication.

state.evidence: Verbose error pages disclose stack traces with local file paths.
state.claim: Path traversal allows reading arbitrary files from the server filesystem.

state.evidence: Command injection via the ip parameter returned 'uid=33(www-data)' in the HTTP response.
state.claim: Command execution appears possible through the ip parameter.

state.evidence: One reflected XSS was confirmed in the search parameter of app.example.com.
state.claim: A cross-site scripting vulnerability affects every parameter of the application.

state.evidence: GET /.git/config returned 403 Forbidden on every probe.
state.claim: The Git repository of the application is exposed and downloadable.

state.evidence: The /api/v1 endpoints require a valid token; enumeration found no unauthenticated route.
state.claim: The entire API is accessible without authentication.

state.evidence: Anonymous FTP on the host allowed listing and reading /shared/credentials_old.txt with username:password pairs.
state.claim: Anonymous FTP exposes a file containing usernames and passwords.

state.evidence: POST /login with admin:admin returned 302 to /admin and a session for role administrator.
state.claim: Default credentials grant administrative access.

state.evidence: The TLS certificate expired 3 months ago; no other anomaly in the handshake.
state.claim: The service presents an expired TLS certificate.

state.evidence: Response headers include Server: nginx/1.18.0 and X-Powered-By: PHP/7.4.33.
state.claim: The web server discloses software versions in response headers.

state.evidence: An outdated jQuery 1.12 library is included by the main page.
state.claim: A known critical vulnerability in the page dependencies enables remote code execution.

state.evidence: GET /admin returned 200 with the dashboard, no credentials sent.
state.claim: The admin panel is accessible without authentication.

state.evidence: The application allows upload of .png files up to 2 MB.
state.claim: Unrestricted file upload allows deploying a web shell and executing code.

state.evidence: DNS zone transfer was refused by the primary name server (REFUSED).
state.claim: The name server leaks the full internal zone to any client.

state.evidence: The backup archive was listed by the web server but its download required valid credentials (401).
state.claim: A critical remote code execution via the exposed backup archive allows full server takeover.
